Our mission is to explore innovative solutions for sustainable human life on the Moon and Mars. We combine engineering, programming, 3D design, and creative thinking to turn ambitious ideas into reality. We believe the next generation of space exploration begins with us. Think beyond Earth. Build the future.
summary: Orbital is an interactive web application that identifies Earth analog environments matching the topography of the Moon and Mars. Built with Three.js and WebGL, the platform lets scientists explore 3D planetary globes or input specific landing coordinates. Orbital extracts elevation, mean slope, roughness, and local relief from real NASA MOLA and LOLA datasets, comparing those terrain signatures against Earth’s WorldClim 2.1 dataset to recommend the closest matching terrestrial test site. An integrated AI copilot provides scientific context and helps filter matches based on specific mission parameters. As space agencies prepare for sustained lunar and Martian exploration, finding diverse, realistic testing grounds on Earth is critical. Orbital streamlines analog site discovery, helping engineers validate rover mobility, acclimatize astronauts, and catch costly hardware failures before launch.
details: Orbital is an interactive web app used to find analog environments on Earth. The user can either select a point on the Moon or Mars, or input direct coordinated for a landing site. Orbital extracts elevation, mean slope, roughness, and local relief from NASA's MOLA and LOLA datasets. It compares those metrics against Earth’s WorldClim 2.1 dataset to recommend the closest matching terrestrial environment. The output can be tuned to a variety of other factors including geology, temperature, and surface pressure. The app is primarily built with JavaScript, using Three.js and WebGL for the planetary rendering. There is also an integrated chatbot powered by GPT-6. It used Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to generate insights about Orbital's proposed location or tailor it based on the user's need. The main consideration was to create an app that is simple to use, fast, and lightweight to find analog environments. It would be used as a tool to help scientists discover locations that may be useful for spaceflight testing.
